newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols erode as futures stall.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols erode as futures stall.

text.p: Interest rate option implied volatilities eased while the underlying futures traded quietly, posting mild gains on the day.
As traders covered their short positions in futures before the monthly U.S. employment report Friday, options participants likewise were treading cautiously ahead of the closely watched data.
"Most people are staying out of the way until Friday," said a floor broker in Eurodollar options.
One-by-two put spreads were proving popular in Eurodollars as a way of betting on a limited continuation of the downtrend, options traders said.
The strategy, they said, is consistent with market sentiment favoring a single additional rate hike to accompany last month's 25 basis point tightening.
On a one-by-two put spread, the investor buys puts that are near the strike price while selling double the amount of puts at the next strike below at the money.

One of the largest transactions in Eurodollar options during today's session was a Japanese bank's purchase of 8,000 September 95.00 calls at a 1/2-basis-point premium, most likely to cover a previously set short position, observers said.
In bonds, the day's biggest trade was a U.S. bank's sale of 5,000 June 110 calls at 30/64, bond options traders said.
May bond volatility slipped 0.1 point from the previous day to 9.25 percent, and June declined 0.2 to 9.15 percent.
Eurodollar volatility shed 0.1 to 0.3 point across the curve, with the short-dated mid-curves hit even harder, traders said.

For quarterly options, June was pegged at 7.8 percent, with September at 11.30, December at 12.70, March at 13.70, June 1998 at 15.10 and September 1998 at 16.00. June mid-curve volatility was estimated at 16.25 percent and September at 16.30.
